Previously known as '''Bill Walker''',{{cite web|title=NBA.com – Bill Walker Draft 2008 Profile|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2008/profiles/BillWalker.html|access-date=November 3, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091202223850/http://www.nba.com/draft2008/profiles/BillWalker.html|archive-date=December 2, 2009|url-status=dead}} the 6-foot-6-inch-tall (1.98 m) player was selected out of [[Kansas State University]] by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 47th overall pick in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] and traded shortly thereafter to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for cash considerations. ==High school career== Walker was a three-year starter at [[North College Hill High School]] in [[North College Hill, Ohio]], where he was a consensus Top 10 high school recruit{{cite web|title=ScoutHoops.com – 2007 College Basketball Recruiting|work=Scout.com|url=http://www.scout.com/player/50352-bill-walker?s=75|access-date=November 3, 2006}} and a teammate of future NBA lottery pick [[O. J. Mayo]]. His achievements include: * 2006 Second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]{{cite web|title=PARADE Magazine – All-America Teams |work=Parade.com |url=http://all-americans.parade.com/2006_boy_basketball/2006_boys_basketball.html |access-date=November 3, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090212130829/http://all-americans.parade.com/2006_boy_basketball/2006_boys_basketball.html |archive-date=February 12, 2009 }} * 2006 [[USA Today]] All-USA High School Boys' Basketball All-Junior Team{{cite web|title=Breaking news: Walker eligible to compete for K-State mid-year |work=KStateCollegian.com |url=http://media.www.kstatecollegian.com/media/storage/paper1022/news/2006/11/03/News/Breaking.News.Walker.Eligible.To.Compete.For.KState.MidYear-2438557.shtml |date=November 3, 2006 |access-date=November 3, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070513213008/http://media.www.kstatecollegian.com/media/storage/paper1022/news/2006/11/03/News/Breaking.News.Walker.Eligible.To.Compete.For.KState.MidYear-2438557.shtml |archive-date=May 13, 2007 }} * 2006 [[EA Sports]] High School Boys' Basketball First Team{{cite web|title=2006 EA SPORTS Boys All American Team|work=Rivals.com|url=https://ssbasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1132&CID=537673|access-date=July 10, 2006}} * [[Ohio]] High School Basketball Coaches Association All-State First Team * [[Cincinnati Enquirer]] All-State First Team As a sophomore and junior in 2005 and 2006, Walker helped North College Hill to back-to-back Ohio Division III state titles and was named the Most Valuable Player of the 2006 State Tournament. In 2006, North College Hill finished third in the USA Today Super 25 High School rankings,{{cite web|first=Christopher|last=Lawlor|title=Final Super 25 boys' basketball rankings|work=USAToday.com|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2006-final-super25.htm|date=March 27, 2006|access-date=March 27, 2006}} with Walker averaging 21.7 points and 10.1 rebounds per game. He was selected the USA Today National Player of the Week on March 27, 2006. In the fall of 2006, Walker graduated early after it was ruled that he had used all of his high school athletics eligibility the previous year.{{cite web|title=Ohio rules prep hoops standout Bill Walker ineligible|work=USAToday.com|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2006-07-10-walker-ineligible_x.htm|date=July 10, 2006|access-date=July 10, 2006}} Walker also helped the USA White team to a 5–0 record at the 2005 USA Youth Development Festival in [[San Diego, California]], where he played alongside [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] freshman [[Greg Oden]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] freshman [[Darrell Arthur]]. He was the only three-time [[Most Valuable Player]] at the [[Reebok]] [[ABCD Camp]] in [[Teaneck, New Jersey]]. ==College career== After receiving interest from many [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] teams, including [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|Southern California]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], Walker enrolled at [[Kansas State University]] as a part-time student in order to be eligible to play on December 16, 2006, the start of the second semester. He had an immediate impact on the team, averaging 11.3 points and 4.5 rebounds per game in his first six games. However, he [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ruptured]] the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) in his left knee early in a game against [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] on January 6, 2007, which required surgery and abruptly ended his freshman season.{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Katz|title=Walker's season comes to an end with ruptured ACL|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2724691|date=January 9, 2007|access-date=January 9, 2007}} This was the second time he suffered this type of injury, going through surgery and rehab in his right knee in 2003. In the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007–08]] season, Walker averaged 16.1 points and 6.3 rebounds in 31 games. He tied his career-high with 31 points in a 92–86 loss at [[Baylor Bears#Basketball|Baylor]] on February 23, 2008, and combined with teammate [[Michael Beasley]] to score 75 of the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]]' 86 points in that game. On April 14, 2008, Walker announced along with Beasley that he would enter the 2008 NBA draft and thus forgo his last three years of eligibility.{{cite web|first=Howard |last=Richman |title=Beasley, Walker declare for NBA draft |work=KansasCity.com |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/story/575088.html |date=April 14, 2008 |access-date=April 14, 2008 |url-status=dead
